body:
Two throughput items, one of which needs you and one of which is just sharp.

1. FIVE BATCH MEMBERS HAVE NO `execution_mode`, SO THEY CANNOT AUTO-MERGE.

    BUG-1442  BUG-1445  BUG-1450  BUG-1452  BUG-1454     (5 of 23 members)

BUG-1445 just demonstrated the consequence at 20:20:45:

    AdvisorEscalated — "BUG-1445 is marked unset (supervised) — auto-merge refused;
                        merge requires human/advisor review"
    PhaseDonePr pr=2028

So the drain did the whole job — implementer, CI, review — opened PR #2028, and then handed it to you because the spec has no mode. Ungroomed specs are not skipped; they are driven to completion and then parked at the merge gate. Every one adds to a hold queue that is already fourteen deep, and the work is already done by the time it lands there.

That makes grooming those five the cheapest throughput action available right now: five `execution_mode` writes, and four of them are already past the expensive phases. It is your call what mode each gets — I am not setting modes from this seat — but the ordering argument is that these are nearly-finished work sitting one field away from landing.

Worth noting the message renders the absent mode as the literal string "unset" — "BUG-1445 is marked unset (supervised)" reads as though `unset` were a mode someone chose. Minor, but it is a diagnostic printing an internal sentinel to a human. Not filing it; mentioning in case it is one line to fix in whatever touches BUG-1485.

2. BUG-1476 HIT THE LEASE MISMATCH ON ITS FIRST PICKUP, WHICH IS THE COMPOUNDING CASE.

I reordered the implementer queue so the throughput fixes go first. BUG-1476 is now slot 1, picked up at 20:20:48, and at 20:21:25 — thirty-seven seconds in — it hit "could not match the orchestrated session to a session lease", attempt 2/2. Fifth occurrence of BUG-1485, and it is now blocking the spec that fixes the rework loop.

Attempt 2 is running as I write. BUG-1445 recovered on its second attempt and produced PR #2028, so this is survivable rather than fatal. But the shape is worth naming: BUG-1485 is the defect most likely to prevent BUG-1476 from ever being worked, and BUG-1476 is the fix that makes every subsequent rework round capable of producing a commit. They are the top two slots for that reason and I would not reorder them further.

If BUG-1476 burns both attempts, I will not requeue it blind — per its own finding, a requeued spec with an open PR no-ops in fifteen seconds. If it fails I will come back to you rather than loop it.

QUEUE HEAD, for the record:

    1. BUG-1476  rework rounds produce no commit
    2. BUG-1485  lease mismatch strands pushed work
    3. BUG-1447  branch-protection misclassified as merge conflict
    4. BUG-1480  aida show 7.5s on a healthy cache
    5. BUG-1460  reviewer phase before terminal CI
    6. BUG-1470  reviewed specs never re-driven
    7. BUG-1467  verdicts written without reviewed_sha

Thank you for grooming 1485, 1480 and 1467 that fast — all three were approved and batched before I went looking for them.
